title: How does image generation work?
reading: The slide introduces diffusion models as the mechanism behind image generation: Gaussian noise is gradually added to an image, and a model learns to reverse that corruption. A horizontal figure below illustrates the two directions of the process using a puppy photograph at varying noise levels.

visuals.description: A row of three images — pure colored noise on the left, a heavily noised puppy in the middle, a clean puppy photo on the right — separated by ellipses. A red arrow above points left-to-right labeled 'Denoising/generation process'; a red arrow below points right-to-left labeled 'Diffusion process'.
visuals.assertion: The forward diffusion process destroys a clean image into noise step by step, while the learned reverse (denoising) process generates an image from noise.

concepts.name: Diffusion models
concepts.why_it_matters: Core generative framework: add noise, then learn its reversal.

concepts.name: Gaussian noise
concepts.why_it_matters: The corruption used in the forward process.

concepts.name: Denoising/generation process
concepts.why_it_matters: The learned reverse direction that produces samples.
